sections.h2: What should I know before selling a house in Kannapolis?
sections.html:
Kannapolis sits across two counties, so the first job is to find out which county's records and tax office apply to your parcel. The city lies in Cabarrus County and Rowan County, and the answer changes who bills your property tax and who records your deed.

The Census Bureau estimates 61,708 residents for July 1, 2025, up from 53,114 counted in the 2020 census and 42,625 in 2010. That kind of growth means plenty of buyers are looking, and it also means neighbors, new construction and older mill-era streets all compete for attention when you set a price. Selling in Kannapolis usually comes down to three routes: list with an agent, sell it yourself, or accept a cash offer for the house as it stands.

sections.h2: How did Kannapolis grow, and why does that matter for an older house?
sections.html:
Kannapolis began as a mill village, and many of its oldest houses date from that period. According to the city's history page, J.W. Cannon bought land in 1906 that later became Kannapolis, acquiring 1,008 acres across Cabarrus and Rowan Counties, and the Cannon Manufacturing mill began production in 1908. Cannon Mills built roughly 1,600 homes for its employees, along with a YMCA, civic center and daycare.

The city incorporated in 1984. In July 2003 the Pillowtex closing put 4,340 people out of work in what the city calls the largest one-day layoff in North Carolina history. In 2004 a plan was announced for the North Carolina Research Campus, which the city describes as a $1.5 billion project now home to eight universities, a community college program and several nutrition and health employers.

For a seller, this history shows up in the houses themselves. A small mill-era home, a 1990s subdivision house and a newer build near the research campus attract different buyers. If yours has an older roof, original wiring or deferred repairs, a buyer who purchases as-is can save you the repair-and-inspection cycle that traditional buyers often request.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers say about housing in Kannapolis?
sections.html:
Kannapolis is mostly owner-occupied, with a median home value of $276,400 for 2020 to 2024 according to Census QuickFacts. The table below collects the figures most useful to a seller.

The same release shows 89.2% of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, so most households stay put. The median monthly owner cost is $1,603 with a mortgage and $486 without one. These are medians for the whole city, so they describe a typical Kannapolis home and say little about your block.

sections.h2: Which county bills property tax on a Kannapolis house?
sections.html:
The county where your parcel sits bills it, which is either Cabarrus County or Rowan County. Check the tax bill or the county's online parcel search to see which one lists your property, and call that county's tax office with questions.

Cabarrus County revalues real estate every four years, a shorter cycle than the eight years North Carolina requires. Its revaluation FAQ says each property was valued at its fair market value as of January 1, 2024, and that the size of the change from one revaluation to the next is not a valid reason for appeal. Tax bills are typically mailed in late July or early August, are due September 1 and are considered past due if not paid before January 5. Rates come from the county commissioners and each taxing jurisdiction, and the county says they are usually finalized in June.

  • The bill goes to the owner as of January 1 of the tax year.
  • If you sold the property, the county asks you to forward the bill to the new owner.
  • Under state law, interest starts on unpaid taxes after the January 5 window and runs at 2% for the first weeks, then three-fourths of one percent each month.

sections.h2: How can I appeal a Cabarrus County value before I sell?
sections.html:
Send a written request for an informal review to Cabarrus County Tax Administration, and include whatever supports your case, such as comparable sales or photos of problems. The county says nothing specific is required, but better documentation makes the review more effective.

An appraiser reviews what you send and returns a notice titled Informal Review. If you disagree, you have 30 days from that response notice to continue to a formal appeal. State law sends formal appeals first to the county board of equalization and review, which is made up of the county commissioners unless a special board is created. A further appeal to the Property Tax Commission must be filed within 30 days after the board mails its decision.

A lower assessed value helps you only while you own the home, but it can also support your asking price conversation, since buyers can read the county card for any parcel. For Rowan County parcels, ask the Rowan County tax office for its current revaluation schedule and appeal steps.

sections.h2: What recording and closing steps apply to a Kannapolis sale?
sections.html:
Your deed is recorded with the register of deeds in the county where the land lies, so Kannapolis sellers use either the Cabarrus or the Rowan office. State law puts the excise tax on the seller: $1.00 for each $500 of consideration or fraction of it, paid to the register of deeds before the deed is recorded. Recording matters because an unrecorded conveyance generally does not protect a buyer against lien creditors or other purchasers.

  • Statewide recording fee for an ordinary instrument: $26.00 for the first 15 pages, plus $4.00 for each extra page.
  • Deeds of trust and mortgages: $64.00 for the first 35 pages, plus $4.00 per added page.
  • No fee to record the satisfaction or cancellation of a mortgage or deed of trust.

Ask your closing attorney or title company to confirm which charges fall on you in your contract. The statute sets the tax and fees, but the contract and the title company set who pays what at the table.

sections.h2: What happens if a Kannapolis house is behind on mortgage payments?
sections.html:
North Carolina foreclosures run through a hearing before the clerk of superior court, and you often have time to sell before a sale closes. The foreclosing party files a notice of hearing, and the hearing is held in the county where the land lies. The notice must be served at least 10 days before the hearing.

  • The clerk must find a valid debt, a default, a right to foreclose and proper notice.
  • An appeal of the clerk's finding goes to a judge within 10 days, and an owner-occupant's bond is 1% of the principal balance unless reduced.
  • After a foreclosure sale, an upset bid must top the reported price by at least 5% with a $750 minimum increase, and each upset bid opens a new 10-day period.

If you are in this position, a payoff statement from your lender and a title search tell you how much equity is left before you compare offers.

sections.h2: Which way of selling fits a Kannapolis homeowner best?
sections.html:
The right route depends on the condition of the house, your timeline and how much equity you want to keep. A traditional listing can bring the widest buyer pool, but it brings showings, repair requests and agent fees. A cash purchase of the house as-is trades some price flexibility for a shorter, more predictable process.

  • List with an agent when the house is in good shape and you can wait through showings and a buyer's financing.
  • Sell it yourself if you are comfortable handling pricing, disclosures and contracts.
  • Take a cash offer when you want to skip repairs, deal with tenants or inherited property, or sell before a foreclosure date.

Compare written offers, ask each buyer who pays closing costs and the recording fees, and keep the signed contract terms in front of you.

faqs.q: Is Kannapolis in Cabarrus County or Rowan County?
faqs.a: Both. The city history page says the land Cannon bought lay in Cabarrus and Rowan Counties, and the city still spans the two. Look at your tax bill to see which county lists your parcel, then use that county's tax office and register of deeds.

faqs.q: Who pays the deed excise tax when a Kannapolis house sells?
faqs.a: The seller pays it under North Carolina law. It is $1.00 per $500 of the price or value, collected by the register of deeds before the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: When are Cabarrus County property taxes due?
faqs.a: September 1. Cabarrus County's FAQ says bills are past due if not paid before January 5. The bill follows the owner as of January 1, so forward it to the buyer if you sold.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Kannapolis house with unpaid taxes or a mortgage in default?
faqs.a: Yes, in many cases. Taxes and liens are normally paid from the sale proceeds at closing, and a payoff letter shows the amounts. For a house facing foreclosure, the hearing before the clerk and the upset bid period can leave time to close a sale.

faqs.q: What is a typical home value in Kannapolis?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau lists $276,400 as the median value of owner-occupied homes for 2020 to 2024. Your own house may differ, so compare recent nearby sales and the Cabarrus or Rowan County card for your parcel.
